mechanism_narrative: A sustained 1-month increase in the federal funds rate compresses equity discount rates and reduces forward equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active as it is derived from the monthly change in FEDFUNDS.
failure_condition: The 1-month change in FEDFUNDS does not predict negative 20-day returns: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in periods of FEDFUNDS rise is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL reading above 238.5 (indicating elevated inflation) triggers a negative market reaction as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL above 238.5 does not lead to negative 20-day returns: 20-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4.5% signals a tight labor market, strong economic growth, and low recession risk, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 4.5% does not lead to positive 20-day returns: 20-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal requires both series to exceed their respective thresholds.
failure_condition: HOUST>1200 AND RSAFS>450000 does not lead to positive 20-day returns: 20-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by year-over-year GDP growth above 2.0% and rising), a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active only when the regime condition holds and UNRATE increases.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2.0% YoY AND UNRATE rises
failure_condition: The signal condition (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% YoY AND UNRATE rise) does not lead to negative 20-day returns: 20-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% (indicating a restrictive monetary policy) compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as the market reacts to the tightening.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 4.0% does not lead to negative 5-day returns: 5-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year growth rate in GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% signals a strong economy and robust corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth above 2.0% YoY does not lead to positive 60-day returns: 60-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) and elevated unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) signal a severe economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal requires both conditions to be met.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS>4.0 AND UNRATE>5.0 does not lead to negative 60-day returns: 60-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the hit rate is below 55%.
